name: Math Academy
line: Math Academy places with a test and teaches by lesson. In AMP, assessment, teaching and review happen at every problem.
description: AMP vs Math Academy: Math Academy places with a diagnostic and teaches by lesson. In AMP, assessment, teaching and review are continuous, at every problem.
verdict: Math Academy places a learner with a diagnostic, teaches in lessons that open with a worked example, gives no hints by design, and schedules review as tasks and timed quizzes [3][4][8]. In AMP, assessment, teaching and review are continuous. Every answer updates the learner's level and sets the next problem, and each problem carries its own hint, lesson and worked answer.

reasons.title: Continuous assessment
reasons.body: AMP has no separate test. It places a learner from their first answers, and every answer after updates the learner's level in that part of math and sets the next problem: new work within reach, a gap to close, or an old skill due back. Math Academy places a new learner with an adaptive diagnostic of 30 to 45 minutes [3]. After that, timed quizzes on earlier topics come at intervals, and lesson material is locked while they run [3][4].

reasons.title: The problem is the unit
reasons.body: In AMP, everything a learner needs hangs off the problem in front of them: a hint that gives the first step, a lesson with a worked example, a video lesson, the worked answer afterward, and links to the skills it builds on and leads to. In Math Academy the unit is the lesson: a worked example at each step, then practice problems until two in a row are right [3]. Its lessons are text with diagrams, and the company's book argues that following a video is not learning [3][8].

reasons.title: A hint, recorded as help
reasons.body: In AMP, a hint and a lesson are in reach at every problem. An answer given after either is marked as helped and does not count as learned. A skill counts when the learner gets it right without help, more than once. Math Academy gives no hints by design. Its book argues that the system should not lower the bar by "giving away hints" [8]. A learner who misses reads the explanation and gets more problems, and after too many misses the lesson halts and comes back later [4][8].

reasons.title: Continuous review
reasons.body: In AMP, learned skills come back in ordinary practice, at growing intervals, mixed with other math. Math Academy schedules review for each student and topic, as review tasks and timed quizzes, and counts advanced work as partial review of the simpler skills inside it [3][4]. In a randomized trial with 787 seventh graders, mixed and spaced practice scored 61% on a surprise test a month later, against 38% for practice in blocks [13].

reasons.title: One program from counting
reasons.body: AMP is one program from counting through precalculus, on one map of skills, with a separate level for each part of math. A learner further along in one part than another gets work at both levels. Math Academy's courses begin at the 4th grade level. A new learner needs multiplication facts through 12 and must be able to read independently [2][6].

rows.range: Grade 4 math through AP Calculus and university courses. A new learner needs multiplication facts through 12 and independent reading [1][6].
rows.start: A separate adaptive diagnostic of about 30 to 45 minutes, which also checks earlier foundations. Very slow correct answers count for less [3][4].
rows.teaching: Text lessons with diagrams, each step opening with a worked example. Every question has an explanation. No hints, by design [3][8].
rows.next: An algorithm chooses tasks over a map of prerequisites. The learner picks among the lessons, reviews and quizzes it offers [3][4].
rows.mastery: Two right in a row at each step of a lesson. Too many misses halt the lesson for a later retry [3][4].
rows.review: Review tasks scheduled per student and topic, and timed quizzes on earlier topics. Advanced work counts as partial review of simpler skills [3][4].
rows.print: None found in the pages we read. Learners work online, with scratch paper [1][2].
rows.adult: The system chooses and grades the work. The adult can set XP goals, workdays and breaks [2][3].
rows.reports: Daily activity and progress, notifications and a diagnostic report. Transcripts with grades and certificates of completion [1][2][3].
rows.evidence: No outcome study found on its site, in Evidence for ESSA's math programs or in the What Works Clearinghouse product list [1][10][12].

theirs: Math Academy is an online math program from Math Academy, LLC [1]. It grew out of an accelerated math program in Pasadena's public schools, which still runs on it [7]. Courses run from 4th grade math through AP Calculus and university courses such as linear algebra and differential equations [1][6]. The company sets out its method in a book, The Math Academy Way [8].

A new learner starts with an adaptive diagnostic [3]. An algorithm then chooses tasks over a map of prerequisites, and each day the learner picks from them: lessons, reviews, multistep problems and quizzes [3][4]. A lesson opens with a worked example and gives practice problems at each step. Two right in a row moves on [3]. Review is scheduled for each student and topic, and timed quizzes on earlier topics come at intervals [3][4]. Work is counted in XP, about one XP per focused minute [2].
credit: A map of prerequisites, with review scheduled for each student and topic, and advanced work counted as partial review of the simpler skills inside it [4].
Each lesson step opens with a fully worked example, and every question has an explanation [3].
A learner who keeps missing a lesson gets remedial review of its key prerequisites [4].

theirs: We found no outcome study of Math Academy, randomized or with a comparison group, on its site, in Evidence for ESSA's math programs or in the What Works Clearinghouse product list [1][5][10][12]. Evidence for ESSA rates My Math Academy Strong, but that is a different product, for preschool and kindergarten, from another company, Age of Learning [11].

Math Academy's pedagogy page cites general research on mastery learning, spacing and interleaving. None of those studies tested Math Academy [5]. Its claim of learning at four times the speed of a regular class compares the minutes in its courses with an estimate of class and homework time, not learning against a comparison group [1][2][8]. Justin Skycak, who wrote the company's book, reports that students in the Pasadena school program were invited after scoring at or above the 90th percentile on a middle school math placement exam, and that most who took AP Calculus BC in eighth grade passed. The post gives no counts [9].
ours: Two findings bear on both programs. Worked examples improve math performance, with an average effect of g = 0.48 across 55 studies [14]. In a randomized trial with 787 seventh graders, mixed and spaced practice scored 61% on a surprise test a month later, against 38% for practice in blocks [13]. AMP applies both at every problem.

AMP's own outcome studies are planned: growth on a national test against hours of use, then comparison groups, then randomized trials. Each will be registered before it starts and published whatever it finds. The research behind each part of AMP is in our report, and AMP is open source.

them: Your learner reads independently, knows multiplication facts through 12, and wants to learn lesson by lesson from worked examples, without hints.
amp: You want assessment, teaching and review in the same practice, with no separate tests.
You want a hint that gives the first step when your child is stuck, with the helped answer recorded.
Your child is starting with counting.
You want printable workbooks made from your child's own record, with worked answer keys.
You want to see the actual problems behind every number.

questions.question: How is AMP different from Math Academy?
questions.answer: Math Academy places a learner with a diagnostic, teaches in lessons that open with a worked example, and gives no hints by design [3][8]. AMP has no separate test: every answer sets the next problem, each problem carries its own hint, lesson and worked answer, and learned skills return in ordinary practice.

questions.question: Does Math Academy work?
questions.answer: We found no outcome study of Math Academy on its site, in Evidence for ESSA's math programs or in the What Works Clearinghouse product list [1][10][12]. The results it reports come from its own data, including a selective school program [9].

questions.question: Can a learner use both?
questions.answer: Yes. They are separate programs. AMP places a learner from their first answers, whatever else they use.
